newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cetes rates drop, signal warning on peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cetes rates drop, signal warning on peso.

text.p: Mexico's treasury bill rates posted sharp declines across the yield curve at Banco de Mexico's primary auction on Tuesday, but the steep drop in short-term has raised a warning for the peso, analysts said.
The bellwether 28-day Cetes rate fell for the eighth straight week, declining by a greater-than-expected 176 basis points to 19.69 percent.
A strong inflow of dollars into Mexican markets has helped push down the treasury bill rates, analysts said.

But the sharp steepening in the yield curve as short-term rates decline can drive investors out to the longer end, and eventually right out of the market, which has the potential to weaken the peso, IDEA economist Gene Frieda told Reuters.
"Value has been soaked up in the short-end so people run out in a last-ditch effort to get yield. All of sudden there is no value left and people leave," he said.

One indicator they monitor is the ratio of one-year to one-month Cetes rates, and a high ratio, such as the one seen now, has in the past worked as a leading indicator of impending peso weakness, he said.
Frieda added, however, that market players are likely to find a bit more value in both Cetes and the peso before any sell-off.
Mexican markets have been strong recently on inflows of capital, particularly into the stock market which ended Tuesday on a record high of 3,750.03 points - a rise of 1.93 percent.
Mexican peso contracts also strengthened across the board on Tuesday as foreign investors flooded into the stock and money markets.

"We have said before that we thought interest rates were nearing a floor, but the heavy inflows of foreign funds has been a factor that has allowed the trend towards lower rates to continue," brokerage house Banorte said in report.
The one-month Cetes rate hit 29.89 percent in mid-November last year, fell, then rose again to 27.37 percent on December 17. Since then the bellweather one-month rate has fallen steadily.
A survey of nine money market dealers earlier on Tuesday found expectations of a decline of 115 basis points to 20.30 percent on the 28-day Cetes.

"These are levels (after Tuesday's auction) that we thought we would see in August, when we had lower inflation and had passed through the electoral period in July", said Banco Union economist Ricardo Vazquez.
Inflation in January was 2.57 percent, but economists have said that there is clear evidence inflationary pressures were easing.
Demand this week was a strong 13.36 billion pesos, compared to 12.72 billion pesos last week.
At the auction on Tuesday, the rate on the three-month paper fell 107 basis points to 22.14 percent, while the six-month paper showed a decline of 131 basis points to 22.75 percent.
The yield on one-year paper was 23.99 percent, compared to 25.30 percent last week.
